commit.message: fix(runtime): fence SADHANA crash recovery authority

this_packet_provides: generic TaskBoard mutation fence for typed campaign and recovery authority
exact live-attempt terminal TaskBoard projection compare-and-swap
complete new-claim ExecutionIdentity metadata for a caller-owned Board carrier
monotone terminal runtime claim/run replay and canonical retry lineage
atomic hook for terminal runtime outbox preparation
consumer_provides: production orchestrator persistence of the complete ExecutionIdentity into the exact Board claim assignment before provider execution
DharmaGraph authority snapshot and replayable projection metadata
effect-indeterminate crash holds and receipt-driven reconciliation
cross_packet_interface.shared_proof: After the governed consumer persists the complete returned identity before effects, process loss cannot remint attempt authority; an exact later receipt can converge runtime and TaskBoard truth without erasing lineage.

interface_mismatches: Generic TaskBoard status and metadata APIs previously accepted campaign rows and could erase, fabricate, or recreate typed attempt authority.
Task metadata from a prior claim could be reused as the execution identity of a newly claimed retry, and required paths accepted missing incoming custody.
Runtime claim/run upserts could replay an open status over a terminal row, erasing a prepared projection, and retry run rows could omit the identity parent lineage.
Runtime terminalization had no same-transaction hook for the existing-store TaskBoard projection outbox.

The production orchestrator currently prepares Board claim metadata before identity construction; the sibling DharmaGraph/orchestrator packet must persist this packet's complete identity metadata into the Board assignment before any campaign effect.
Runtime SQLite and TaskBoard SQLite remain separate stores; convergence must be replayable and idempotent rather than falsely described as cross-database atomic.

Legacy fail-closed recovery tests synthesized corrupt terminal claim/run rows through generic public writers; those fixtures must now seed the impossible persisted state directly below the guarded API.
honest_blockers: The current production orchestrator writes claim metadata prepared before identity construction. Campaign dispatch must remain stopped until the sibling DharmaGraph/orchestrator packet persists this packet's complete identity metadata into the exact Board assignment.
This packet does not itself settle a TaskBoard row from a runtime receipt; the sibling DharmaGraph packet supplies and verifies projection authority and replay.
An in-flight campaign provider effect without a bound terminal receipt remains effect-indeterminate and cannot authorize retry.
Runtime SQLite and TaskBoard SQLite cannot form one transaction; later convergence remains exact, replayable, and receipt-bound.

This proves local runtime and TaskBoard mechanics only, not production orchestrator persistence, provider authenticity, useful output, Mission Control projection, deployment, iPhone access, or campaign completion.

Adversarial Mission Control fixtures write corrupt or unverified metadata and terminal lifecycle rows directly below public RuntimeState/TaskBoard APIs solely to prove downstream fail-closed behavior; those writes are test-only and grant no runtime authority.
No external service, VPS, provider, public route, or Git remote may be mutated by this packet.
session_entry.rollback: Keep campaign dispatch stopped, preserve runtime.db and tasks.db for forensic reconciliation, and revert this private branch commit before the DharmaGraph consumer is activated. Reverting restores generic mutation behavior, so no campaign dispatch may resume until equivalent typed fences plus the consumer-owned production identity persistence seam are present.
